items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: I went to Mr. Boyd for I guess maybe four or five months.

ctx.x: That turned out to be a very good thing to me, and I am always grateful to my father for having done that. I was glad that he had had the foresight to take me away from this other fellow, who was a good pianist himself, but the way he was teaching me, without the basics of any music... Because when he came in, he didn't have not a sheet of music, less more a book. He was just showing me stuff that he was doing on the keyboard, which if I had continued this, I guess it would have made quite a difference in my…

I went to Mr. Boyd for I guess maybe four or five months. And, like all youngsters, you learn a little bit of something and you think you know something. Meanwhile, I was at home. I was playing every day, playing what he had taught me and trying to go beyond that, finding other chords and learning
